numbering: Standard 700-verse canon; Chapter 13 has 34 verses and excludes Arjuna's alternate opening question.
sourceChapterWithLineNumbers:
1:   Krishna.
2:   Fearlessness, singleness of soul, the will
3:   Always to strive for wisdom; opened hand
4:   And governed appetites; and piety,
5:   And love of lonely study; humbleness,
6:   Uprightness, heed to injure nought which lives,
7:   Truthfulness, slowness unto wrath, a mind
8:   That lightly letteth go what others prize;
9:   And equanimity, and charity
10:   Which spieth no man's faults; and tenderness
11:   Towards all that suffer; a contented heart,
12:   Fluttered by no desires; a bearing mild,
13:   Modest, and grave, with manhood nobly mixed,
14:   With patience, fortitude, and purity;
15:   An unrevengeful spirit, never given
16:   To rate itself too high;--such be the signs,
17:   O Indian Prince! of him whose feet are set
18:   On that fair path which leads to heavenly birth!
19: 
20:   Deceitfulness, and arrogance, and pride,
21:   Quickness to anger, harsh and evil speech,
22:   And ignorance, to its own darkness blind,--
23:   These be the signs, My Prince! of him whose birth
24:   Is fated for the regions of the vile.[FN#32]
25: 
26:   The Heavenly Birth brings to deliverance,
27:   So should'st thou know! The birth with Asuras
28:   Brings into bondage. Be thou joyous, Prince!
29:   Whose lot is set apart for heavenly Birth.
30: 
31:   Two stamps there are marked on all living men,
32:   Divine and Undivine; I spake to thee
33:   By what marks thou shouldst know the Heavenly Man,
34:   Hear from me now of the Unheavenly!
35: 
36:   They comprehend not, the Unheavenly,
37:   How Souls go forth from Me; nor how they come
38:   Back unto Me: nor is there Truth in these,
39:   Nor purity, nor rule of Life. "This world
40:   Hath not a Law, nor Order, nor a Lord,"
41:   So say they: "nor hath risen up by Cause
42:   Following on Cause, in perfect purposing,
43:   But is none other than a House of Lust."
44:   And, this thing thinking, all those ruined ones--
45:   Of little wit, dark-minded--give themselves
46:   To evil deeds, the curses of their kind.
47:   Surrendered to desires insatiable,
48:   Full of deceitfulness, folly, and pride,
49:   In blindness cleaving to their errors, caught
50:   Into the sinful course, they trust this lie
51:   As it were true--this lie which leads to death--
52:   Finding in Pleasure all the good which is,
53:   And crying "Here it finisheth!"
54: 
55:   Ensnared
56:   In nooses of a hundred idle hopes,
57:   Slaves to their passion and their wrath, they buy
58:   Wealth with base deeds, to glut hot appetites;
59:   "Thus much, to-day," they say, "we gained! thereby
60:   Such and such wish of heart shall have its fill;
61:   And this is ours! and th' other shall be ours!
62:   To-day we slew a foe, and we will slay
63:   Our other enemy to-morrow! Look!
64:   Are we not lords? Make we not goodly cheer?
65:   Is not our fortune famous, brave, and great?
66:   Rich are we, proudly born! What other men
67:   Live like to us? Kill, then, for sacrifice!
68:   Cast largesse, and be merry!" So they speak
69:   Darkened by ignorance; and so they fall--
70:   Tossed to and fro with projects, tricked, and bound
71:   In net of black delusion, lost in lusts--
72:   Down to foul Naraka. Conceited, fond,
73:   Stubborn and proud, dead-drunken with the wine
74:   Of wealth, and reckless, all their offerings
75:   Have but a show of reverence, being not made
76:   In piety of ancient faith. Thus vowed
77:   To self-hood, force, insolence, feasting, wrath,
78:   These My blasphemers, in the forms they wear
79:   And in the forms they breed, my foemen are,
80:   Hateful and hating; cruel, evil, vile,
81:   Lowest and least of men, whom I cast down
82:   Again, and yet again, at end of lives,
83:   Into some devilish womb, whence--birth by birth--
84:   The devilish wombs re-spawn them, all beguiled;
85:   And, till they find and worship Me, sweet Prince!
86:   Tread they that Nether Road.
87: 
88:   The Doors of Hell
89:   Are threefold, whereby men to ruin pass,--
90:   The door of Lust, the door of Wrath, the door
91:   Of Avarice. Let a man shun those three!
92:   He who shall turn aside from entering
93:   All those three gates of Narak, wendeth straight
94:   To find his peace, and comes to Swarga's gate.
95: 
96:   .     .     .     .     .     .     .     .     .     .     .     .[FN#33]
97: 
98:   HERE ENDETH CHAPTER XVI. OF THE BHAGAVAD-GITA,
99:   Entitled  "Daivasarasaupadwibhagayog,"
100:   Or "The Book of the Separateness of the Divine and Undivine."

Deceitfulness, and arrogance, and pride,

  And ignorance, to its own darkness blind,--
  These be the signs, My Prince! of him whose birth
  Is fated for the regions of the vile.[FN#32]

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.4 Hypocrisy, arrogance and self-conceit, anger and also harshness and ignorance, belong to one who is born for a demoniacal state, O Partha (Arjuna).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.4 Hypocrisy, pride, insolence, cruelty, ignorance belong to him who is born of the godless qualities.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.4 O son of Prtha, (the attributes) of one destined to have the demoniacal nature are religious ostentation, pride and haughtiness, [Another reading is abhimanah, self-conceit.-Tr.], anger as also rudeness and ignorance.

arnold.content:

  Brings into bondage. Be thou joyous, Prince!
  Whose lot is set apart for heavenly Birth.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.5 The divine nature is deemed conducive to liberation, and the demoniacal to bondage. Grieve not, O Arjuna, thou art born with divine endowments.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.5 Godly qualities lead to liberation; godless to bondage. Do not be anxious, Prince! Thou hast the Godly qualities.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.5 The divine nature is the Liberation, the demoniacal is considered to be for inevitable bondage. Do not grieve, O son of Pandu! You are destined to have the divine nature.

arnold.content:
Two stamps there are marked on all living men,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.6 There are two types of beings in this world, the divine and the demoniacal; the divine has been described at length; hear from Me, O Arjuna, of the demoniacal.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.6 All beings are of two classes: Godly and godless. The Godly I have described; I will now describe the other.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.6 In this world there are are two (kinds of) creation of beings: the divine and the demoniacal. The divine has been spoken of elaborately. Hear about the demoniacal from Me, O son of Prtha.

arnold.content:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.7 The demoniacal know not what to do and what to refrain from; neither purity, nor right conduct nor truth is found in them.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.7 The godless do not know how to act or how to renounce. They have neither purity nor truth. They do not understand the right principles of conduct.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.7 Neither do the demoniacal persons under-stand what is to be done and what is not to be done; nor does purity, or even good conduct or truthfulness exist in them.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.8 They say, "This universe is without truth, without (moral) basis, without a God, brought about by mutual union, with lust for its cause; what else?"

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.8 They say the universe is an accident with no purpose and no God. Life is created by sexual union, a product of lust and nothing else.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.8 They say that the world is unreal, it has no basis, it is without a God. It is born of mutual union brought about by passion! What other (cause can there be)?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.9 Holding on to this view, (these people) who are of depraved character, of poor intellect, given to fearful actions and harmful, wax strong for the ruin of the world.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda

arnold.content:
To-day we slew a foe, and we will slay
  Our other enemy to-morrow! Look!
  Are we not lords? Make we not goodly cheer?
  Is not our fortune famous, brave, and great?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.14 "That enemy has been slain by me; and others also I shall slay. I am the lord. I enjoy. I am perfect, powerful and happy."

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.14 I have slain one enemy, I will slay the others also; I am worthy to enjoy, I am the Almighty, I am perfect, powerful and happy;

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.14 'That enemy has been killed by me, and I shall kill others as well. I am the lord, I am the enjoyer, I am well-established, mighty and happy.'

records.sanskrit:

records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Rich are we, proudly born! What other men
  Live like to us? Kill, then, for sacrifice!
  Cast largesse, and be merry!" So they speak
  Darkened by ignorance;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.15 "I am rich and born in a noble family. Who else is equal to me? I shall perform sacrifices. I shall give (charity). I shall rejoice," thus deluded by ignorance.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.15 I am rich, I am well-bred; who is there to compare with me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will pay - and I will enjoy. Thus blinded by Ignorance,

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.15 'I am rich and high-born; who else is there similar to me? I shall perform sacrifices; I shall give, I shall rejoice,'-thus they are diversely deluded by non-discrimination.

records.sanskrit:
अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः।
प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥
records.iast:
anekacittavibhrāntā mohajālasamāvṛtāḥ
prasaktāḥ kāmabhogeṣu patanti narake.aśucau
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
and so they fall--
  Tossed to and fro with projects, tricked, and bound
  In net of black delusion, lost in lusts--
  Down to foul Naraka.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.16 Bewildered by many a fancy, entangled in the snare of delusion, addicted to the gratification of lust, they fall into a foul hell.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.16 Perplexed by discordant thoughts, entangled in the snares of desire, infatuated by passion, they sink into the horrors of hell.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.16 Bewildered by numerous thoughts, caught in the net of delusion, (and) engrossed in the enjoyment of desirable objects, they fall into a foul hell.

records.sanskrit:
आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः।
यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
records.iast:
ātmasambhāvitāḥ stabdhā dhanamānamadānvitāḥ
yajante nāmayajñaiste dambhenāvidhipūrvakam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Conceited, fond,
  Stubborn and proud, dead-drunken with the wine
  Of wealth, and reckless, all their offerings
  Have but a show of reverence, being not made
  In piety of ancient faith.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.17 Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name out of ostentation, contrary to scriptural ordinances.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.17 Self-conceited, stubborn, rich, proud and insolent, they make a display of their patronage, disregarding the rules of decency.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.17 Self-conceited, haughty, filled with pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices which are so in name only, with ostentation and regardless of the injunctions.

records.sanskrit:
अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः।
मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः ॥
records.iast:
ahaṃkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ
māmātmaparadeheṣu pradviṣanto.abhyasūyakāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Thus vowed
  To self-hood, force, insolence, feasting, wrath,
  These My blasphemers, in the forms they wear
  And in the forms they breed, my foemen are,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.18 Given over to egoism, power, haughtiness, lust and anger, these malicious people hate Me in their own bodies and in those of others.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.18 Puffed up by power and inordinate conceit, swayed by lust and wrath, these wicked people hate Me Who am within them, as I am within all.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.18 Resorting to egotism, power, arrogance, passion and anger, hating Me in their own and others' bodies, (they become) [As the finite verb is missing in the verse, we have supplied 'they become'. S. adds the verb prabhavanti, wax strong, from verse 9, and constructs the last portion thus: '৷৷.the envious ones wax strond.' Following S. S., however, one may combine this verse with the preceding verse by taking 'perform sacrifices' as the finite verb.-Tr.'] envious by nature.

records.sanskrit:
तानहं द्विषतः क्रुरान्संसारेषु नराधमान्।
क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु ॥
records.iast:
tānahaṃ dviṣataḥ krurānsaṃsāreṣu narādhamān
kṣipāmyajasramaśubhānāsurīṣveva yoniṣu
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Hateful and hating; cruel, evil, vile,
  Lowest and least of men, whom I cast down
  Again, and yet again, at end of lives,
  Into some devilish womb,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.19 Those cruel haters, worst among men in the world, I hurl those evil-doers into the wombs of demons only.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.19 Those who thus hate Me, who are cruel, the dregs of mankind, I condemn them to a continuous, miserable and godless rebirth.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.19 I cast for ever those hateful, cruel, evil-doers in the worlds, the vilest of human beings, verily into the demoniacla classes.

records.sanskrit:
आसुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि।
मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् ॥
records.iast:
āsurīṃ yonimāpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani
māmaprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yāntyadhamāṃ gatim
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
whence--birth by birth--
  The devilish wombs re-spawn them, all beguiled;
  And, till they find and worship Me, sweet Prince!
  Tread they that Nether Road.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.20 Entering into demoniacal wombs and deluded, birth after birth, not attaining Me, they thus fall, O Arjuna, into a condition still lower than that.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.20 So reborn, they spend life after life, enveloped in delusion. And they never reach Me, O Prince, but degenerate into still lower forms of life.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.20 Being born among the demoniacal species in births after births, the foods, without ever reaching Me, O son of Kunti, attain conditions lower than that.

records.sanskrit:
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः।
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
records.iast:
trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ
kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The Doors of Hell
  Are threefold, whereby men to ruin pass,--
  The door of Lust, the door of Wrath, the door
  Of Avarice. Let a man shun those three!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.21 Triple is the gate of this hell, destructive of the self lust, anger and greed; therefore one should abandon these three.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.21 The gates of hell are three: lust, wrath and avarice. They destroy the Self. Avoid them.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.21 This door of hell, which is the destroyer of the soul, is of three kinds-passion, anger and also greed. Therefore one should forsake these three.

records.sanskrit:
एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः।
आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
records.iast:
etairvimuktaḥ kaunteya tamodvāraistribhirnaraḥ
ācaratyātmanaḥ śreyastato yāti parāṃ gatim
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
He who shall turn aside from entering
  All those three gates of Narak, wendeth straight
  To find his peace, and comes to Swarga's gate.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.22 A man who is liberated from these three gates to darkness, O Arjuna, practises what is good for him and thus goes to the Supreme Goal.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.22 These are the gates which lead to darkness; if a man avoid them he will ensure his own welfare, and in the end will attain his liberation.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.22 O son of Kunti, a person who is free from these three doors to darkness strives for the good of the soul. Thery he attains the highest Goal.

records.sanskrit:
यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः।
न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम् ॥
records.iast:
yaḥ śāstravidhimutsṛjya vartate kāmakārataḥ
na sa siddhimavāpnoti na sukhaṃ na parāṃ gatim
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: The source ends its rendering after the three gates and liberation from them. Note 33 says 'ten concluding shlokas'; the actual gap in the project's standard 24-verse chapter is 16.23–16.24. Preserve this discrepancy without adding text.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.23 He who, having cast aside the ordinances of the scriptures, acts under the impulse of desire, attains not perfection, nor happiness nor the Supreme Goal.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.23 But he who neglects the commands of the scriptures, and follows the promptings of passion, he does not attain perfection, happiness or the final goal.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.23 Ignoring the precept of the scriptures, he who acts under the impulsion of passion,-he does not attain perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme Goal.

records.sanskrit:
तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ।
ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि ॥
records.iast:
tasmācchāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ te kāryākāryavyavasthitau
jñātvā śāstravidhānoktaṃ karma kartumihārhasi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: The source ends its rendering after the three gates and liberation from them. Note 33 says 'ten concluding shlokas'; the actual gap in the project's standard 24-verse chapter is 16.23–16.24. Preserve this discrepancy without adding text.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 16.24 Therefore, let the scripture be thy authority in determining what ought to be done and what ought not to be done. Having known what is said in the ordinance of the scriptures, thou shouldst act here in this world.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 16.24 Therefore whenever there is doubt whether thou shouldst do a thing or not, let the scriptures guide thy conduct. In the light of the scriptures shouldst thou labour the whole of thy life."

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 16.24 Therefore, the scripture is your authority as regards the determination of what is to be done and what is not to be done. After understanding (your) duty as presented by scriptural injunction, you ought to perform (your duty) here.
